{{For|other differential equations named after Euler|List of things named after Leonhard Euler#Equations}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Euler's differential equation''' is a first-order [[non-linear]] [[ordinary differential equation]], named after [[Leonhard Euler]]. It is given by:<ref>Ince, E. L. "L. 1944 Ordinary Differential Equations." 227.</ref>

:<math>\frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{\sqrt{a_0+a_1y +a_2 y^2 + a_3 y^3 + a_4 y^4}}{\sqrt{a_0+a_1x +a_2 x^2 + a_3 x^3 + a_4 x^4}} = 0</math>

This is a separable equation and the solution is given by the following integral equation:

:<math>\int \frac{dy}{\sqrt{a_0+a_1 y + a_2 y^2 + a_3 y^3 + a_4 y^4}} + \int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{a_0+a_1 x + a_2 x^2 + a_3 x^3 + a_4 x^4}}  = c </math>
